note: Sezen, reading 1 introduced the social cognitive view as one of five theories. This reading works that one theory out in depth, written by Ellen Usher and Dale Schunk. It adds what reading 1 only touched: agency, the kinds of environment a learner can choose or build, how self-regulation develops, and six components that feed it. The big question of these notes is: how do person, behaviour and environment work together when a learner steers herself, and how can teachers help?

The notes follow the seven steps of the reading 3 walk-through on your dashboard, as seven lectures. Lecture 3.1 sets out the theory, 3.2 the environments, 3.3 the three subfunctions, 3.4 the cycle of Figure 2.1, 3.5 development, 3.6 the six components, and 3.7 what is open and what teachers can do. Every lecture ends with the trap. The exam-style questions, memory hooks and games are on your dashboard and in the two Theme 3 practice sets.

friend: "In this view you're not a puppet of your surroundings: you, what you do and where you are all push on each other, and you can steer. Self-regulation means watching yourself, judging that against a standard you care about, and reacting, before, during and after a task. You learn it by watching someone, copying, doing it alone and then adapting it. It runs on your thinking, behaviour, motivation, emotions, the people around you and your environment, and underneath it all is whether you believe you can."
